statement: Lemma DD: on blocks of L = P^{1/4} consecutive odd steps starting at n0, (i) m(n0+2t) = floor(X0 + D t) + O(1) with X0 = n0^{3/2}, D the first X-increment (quadratic drift ≤ 3/2, so defect ≤ 2); (ii) with mu(t) = m0 + A t (A the realized first m-gap) and s(t) = m(t) - mu(t) — a circle-rotation carry sequence floor({X0} + gamma t) + O(1), gamma = D - A — one has v(n0+2t) = floor(mu(t)^{3/2} + (3/2) mu(t)^{1/2} s(t)) + O(1) (Taylor remainder ≍ P^{-1/4}). On P^{1/4}-blocks the nested level-2 data collapses to a bounded-complexity system: smooth affine base plus one rotation orbit amplified by W ≍ P^{3/4}, with block parameters distributed by proven level-≤2 statistics. Substrate of Conjecture EE (the transport inductive step); measured defects ≤ 2 and ≤ 1 at P = 10^4..10^10. Not a K3 bound; Conjectures V and EE stay open.

With rows J-triple-parity-discrepancy and J-four-step-descent-density this proves every depth-4 itinerary word class except OOO*. Proof: Lemma A' gives the exact identity w^{3/2} = m^{3/4} - (3/2) m^{1/4} theta_w + E (0 ≤ E ≤ (3/8)(U-1)^{-1/2}, using U m^{1/4} = m^{3/4} exactly), so the fourth-letter phase is (k/2) n^{9/8} minus one growing sawtooth B theta_w with B = (3k/4) n^{3/8}; B drifts by ≤ 1 on intervals of length P^{5/8}/k, where a shifted-window Fourier expansion in U (mass O(log), partial summation for the moving coefficients) reduces to smooth modes with single-signed curvature ~ k n^{-7/8} (window T = P^{5/16} << k P^{3/8} avoids sign collision for every k ≥ 1); van der Corput II and the balance J = P^{1/8} give N^{7/8+eps}. No differencing and no kernel: the coefficient crosses integers every P^{5/8}/k steps, unlike the OOO* weight (crossings within single steps) — the engine reaches exactly the letters whose phase coefficients grow slower than n. Proposition JJ (the de-randomization obstruction): no laboratory tool transfers Lemma II from almost-every shift to lambda = 0. (i) No second averaging variable: amplitude separation forces |A(p) - A(q)| <= 1 to imply p = q, so the only amplitude-frozen lattice direction is trivial; every available family average (block index, integer base mu_0, the k-family) re-enters the T1-family or the amplitude-product class (Propositions BB, GG, CC). (ii) Inverse self-similarity: any concentration/discrepancy inverse for A{B} mod 1 is a statement about sum e(j A {B}) — the same class with amplitude jA; the class is closed under its own inverse theory. (iii) Metric non-transfer: |dS/dlambda| <= 2 pi A_max L, so S_lambda decorrelates at shift scale 1/A_max ≍ P^{-27/16} (measured: increments 0.06-0.08 sqrt(L) at delta = 0.1/(2 pi A), 0.57-0.74 sqrt(L) at 1/(2 pi A), saturated at 10x); almost-all statements leave ~ eps A_max bad cells and cannot pin lambda = 0. HH at lambda = 0 is a specific-point-in-metric-theory problem (the 'is sqrt(2) normal' species); the instance's special arithmetic A^2 = (9/16) k^2 z re-enters the harmonic toolkit via its known exploitations. Third and final layer of the K3 obstruction (after BB, GG); the K3/HH line is PARKED here.

Proposition CC: no family-averaging method (double large sieve, dispersion, amplification over the mode index k) can by itself bound the depth-5 class count. Every Fourier expansion of the parity places weight ≍ 1/k on the k-th harmonic, so the count needs |K3(k)| = o(N) for each bounded k — the k = 1 term carries weight one — while dispersion controls only k-averages, which do not constrain any individual bounded-k coefficient; the phase u(n) admits no auxiliary amplification family; and the Selberg-majorant route to the pair-count obligation expands into the kernel family itself (circular). The Phase-17 spacing statistics stand as OBSERVATION. Refutes the dispersion route as a completion method, not any equidistribution statement.

Conjecture (formerly Corollary AB; withdrawn from Paper B in Phase 26): the class of starts carrying a uniform power-envelope descent certificate of length at most eight has natural density 29/32. Conditional implication (Proposition J): if for every itinerary word w of length d the class count satisfies |#w(N) - 2^{-d} N| ≤ E_d(N), then the starts with no contracting prefix of length ≤ d number at most (N_d/2^d) N + N_d E_d(N), where N_d counts the length-d words with no contracting prefix. That count is exact: 3^{o_t} ≥ 2^t must hold at every t ≤ d and depends on nothing but (t, o_t), so N_d is a dynamic program over the triangle 0 ≤ o ≤ t ≤ d, in integers. The closed form N_d ≤ 2^d e^{-cd} with c = 2 (log2/log3 - 1/2)^2 > 0.0342 follows by dropping every constraint but t = d and applying Hoeffding to the odd-letter count (o_d ≥ d log2/log3); that closed form is what this row carried until 2026-09-05, and it is lossy by 6.7 at d = 5, 43.6 at d = 40 and 1.3e4 at d = 1600. The loss is not in the rate -- the sharp value is -log rho = 0.034688 against Hoeffding's 0.034285, one part in eighty -- but polynomial: N_d/2^d ~ C rho^d d^{-3/2} with C about 11, the d^{-1/2} for staying nonnegative under the zero-drift tilt and a further d^{-1} because the tilted endpoint sits at height ~sqrt(d) rather than at the origin. Every other start n ≥ 2 has a uniform power-envelope descent certificate within d steps (row J-power-envelope-contraction). Hence all-depth parity equidistribution with power savings (Conjecture K; proved unconditionally for all itineraries of length ≤ 4 — rows J-triple-parity-discrepancy, J-even-branch-third-letter, J-depth4-slow-branch, J-depth4-complete; depth ≥ 5 open) implies that the set of Juggler starts admitting a finite descent certificate has natural density one — the Juggler analogue of the Terras program. E-rooted words have a contracting prefix at length 1, so only O-rooted class bounds are ever consumed. The implication is unconditional; the hypothesis is open beyond the proved cases. Not a termination claim; no unconditional density-one claim. Imported into the finite-dynamics note as Proposition 6.1. The exact count at d = 5 has four survivors -- OOOOO, OOOOE, OOOEO, OOEOO -- hence certificate density 1 - 4/32 = 7/8, which is Paper B Corollary 6.4's figure reached by counting words rather than contractors; d = 6 is 7/8 again, since all eight children survive.

For odd n ≥ 3 with m = floor(n^{3/2}) and v = floor(m^{3/2}): v^{1/2} = n^{9/8} + D(n) with -(3/4) n^{-3/8} - n^{-9/8} ≤ D(n) ≤ 0, where D(n) = -(3/4) theta n^{-3/8} - (1/2) theta_2 m^{-3/4} - E_3 - E_2 by two applications of the linearization pattern of row J-nested-parity-linearization. Every non-smooth term has decaying amplitude, so smoothing the fourth-letter phase (k/2) v^{1/2} to (k/2) n^{9/8} costs only O(k N^{5/8}) cumulatively. Validated by exact scaled-integer arithmetic through n = 10^{12}, worst ratio 0.9970 against supremum 1.

The OOOO* kernel K3 is bounded by differencing the phase c θ₃ first on X-cell b-runs of floor(ΔX) and then increment-linearizing Z = v^{3/2} along a frozen J = floor(ΔY) (Lemma Z1 leftover α = 29/16, then Theorem R). False: (i) those b-runs do not freeze J — floor(ΔY), Δv, and the κ-fixed branch increment floor((m+b+κ)^{3/2}-m^{3/2}) all have mean and max run length 1 at P = 10^4, 10^5, 10^6, while the b-runs themselves have length ≍ P^{1/2}; the raw increment jumps by ≍ P^{3/4} (level-1 carry flicker) and the branched increment still changes by ≍ P^{1/4} ≫ 1 per step; (ii) changing J by 1 reintroduces the W-family at α = 45/16 via ∂F_J/∂J = (3/2)(v+J)^{1/2}, since c · ∂F_J/∂J / ((9/8) n^{45/16}) → 1 (the Phase-12 wall of row J-scale-invariant-R-extension). SWEEP, 15 Sep 2026. The three K3 falsifier rows -- this one, J-scale-invariant-R-extension and J-x1-absorption-K3 -- all rest on run-length scans recorded at P = 10^4, 10^5, 10^6 only. Restoring the OOOO* coefficient c ≍ k z^{1/2} ≍ k n^{27/16} produces a leftover W-family C θ₂ with C = c F_J'(Y) ≍ k n^{29/16} at the identity-step gap, plus an engine-side remainder. Proposition GG: no intra-block harmonic method in the laboratory toolkit bounds the kernel block sums sum_{t<L} e(k C {Theta}) (C ≍ P^{27/16}, Theta the Lemma-FF phase), at any block length L ≤ P. (I) Window drift: any character expansion in the Theta-direction has its Fourier window centered at kC(t), which drifts by kC' ≍ k P^{11/16} per step, so inner sums at fixed harmonic have length < 1 — vacuous, and independent of block length since the drift is per-step in n. (II) Amplitude transfer: floor-splitting e(k floor(C){Theta}) = e(k floor(C) Theta) is exact but its residual double-Fourier collapses back onto the moving-integer phase; the exact identity C theta_3 = (3/4)(z^{1/2} v^{3/2} - z^{3/2}) converts to pure phases whose floor expansions regenerate the alpha = 45/16 W-family; differencing at any order preserves the full amplitude on theta_3-differences (cross-block variance = the T1-family, dead by Proposition BB); interval-splitting needs R ≥ kC cells and its l^1-mass equals the amplitude. Covers the carry-free case (smooth monomials). Both known proof routes to K3 (global toolkit, Proposition BB; intra-block program, this row) are now closed by named mechanisms. Conjectures V, EE, HH are not refuted. Not a termination claim.

Proposition BB: every method in the laboratory toolkit for K3 dies by one of two mechanisms. (I) It needs a frozen first difference of Y = m^{3/2} (copy of R one nesting up; increment-first on X-cells; X1 landing on v or a v-hybrid). Those cells do not exist (Y'' ≍ n^{1/4} > 1; rows J-scale-invariant-R-extension, J-increment-first-K3, J-x1-absorption-K3). (II) It produces a W-family e(C θ₂) with C ≍ n^{45/16} (V2 then invoke R; replace nested floors by smooth powers). This α exceeds Theorem R's engine line 9/4, the spawned Step-3 coefficient is ≍ n^{25/16} > n, and the amplitude itself satisfies C(n+2)-C(n) ~ (405/64) n^{29/16} >> 1, so R's quasi-static windows cannot run even if the engine line moved toward 2. Therefore the toolkit cannot bound K3. Conjecture V (that K3 cancels) is not refuted. Not a termination claim.

Method claim (Phase-13 slogan, Phase 37): the inventory sum e(u w^{3/2}) closes inside P^{23/24} on Lemma X3 runs by treating kappa_w as a Theorem Q / R3 indicator weight, without a new decoration class. False. (i) Lemma X3 freezes J = floor(Delta U), not kappa_w; U' ~ P^{1/8} >> 1, so kappa is a mechanical word of mean run O(1) on X3-interiors (w_carry_run_scan: 2.26, 1.64, 1.88 at P = 10^4, 10^5, 10^6), shorter than the A-process window H ~ P^{5/32}. (ii) Writing w = U - theta_U spawns the sawtooth B = (3u/2) U^{1/2} ~ |u| n^{9/16}; at |u| ~ P^{27/32} one has B ~ P^{45/32} > n and B' ~ P^{13/32} >> 1 (Phase-5 wall; Lemma 3.7 needs T ~ P^{45/32} > P). (iii) Discarding the accumulated carry costs phase P^{73/32} on an X3-run and P^{25/16} after one A-process. Isolated Lemma X5 is not this sum. The length-7 counts are not refuted. Not a termination claim.

Lemma AA2 (Phase 40): on each length-8 quartet parent the AA1 remainder E is a sum of one-signed second-order Taylor remainders. The hardest chains OOEOOEO and OOEOOOE have leading envelope (297/512) x4^{-5/16} ≍ n^{-45/128}; the OOOEO** parents are no larger. Hence |E| ≪ n^{-45/128} (and |E|<1 for n≥51 is the crude corollary). Finite-difference drift satisfies |E'| ≪ n^{-29/128}<1. On the Phase-23 Vaaler range k≤P^{13/384} one has k|E|→0, so discarding e(kE)-1 costs ≪ P^{131/192}, strictly inside the eighth-letter majorant P^{243/256} and the engine line P^{23/24}. The crude |E|<1 discard (cost J_8 P) remains dead. Scaled-integer residuals lie inside the envelopes with no slack through n=3·10^7. Theorem AA stays CONJECTURE (inherits the length-7 row). Not a termination claim.

Lemma FF: on DD-blocks, with F = mu^{3/2} + (3/2) mu^{1/2} s, v = floor(F) + d, e = d - {F}: theta_3 = { mu^{9/4} + (9/4) mu^{5/4} s + (27/32) mu^{1/4} s^2 - (27/128) mu^{-3/4} s^3 + (243/2048) mu^{-7/4} s^4 + ((3/2) mu^{3/4} + (9/8) mu^{-1/4} s - (27/64) mu^{-5/4} s^2) e + (3/8) mu^{-3/4} e^2 } + O(P^{-19/16}), and (3/4) z^{1/2} = (3/4)(mu^{9/8} + (9/8) mu^{1/8} s - (27/128) mu^{-7/8} s^2) + (9/16) F^{-1/4} e + O(P^{-13/16}), modelling the kernel phase u = (3/4) z^{1/2} theta_3 mod 1 to ~P^{-15/16}. The product form multiplies theta_3 model error by z^{1/2} ≍ P^{27/16}, so the expansion must run three orders past sub-unit — the precision budget of the transport cascade. Validated in exact integers at scale 10^48: theta_3 error 5e-11 (P=10^4) down to 4e-25 (P=10^10); u error 2e-4 down to 2e-8. Discharges obligation (γ) of Conjecture EE: the level-3 kernel phase on a block is an explicit closed form in (mu, s, d, {F}); no nesting remains to be modelled. Not a K3 bound; Conjectures V and EE stay open.

Lemma V2: for odd n ≥ 5, v^{3/2} = m^{9/4} - (3/2) m^{3/4} theta_2 + E2 with 0 ≤ E2 ≤ (3/8) v^{-1/2}, where m = floor(n^{3/2}), v = floor(m^{3/2}), theta_2 = {m^{3/2}}. Taylor of (Y - theta_2)^{3/2} at Y. This is the forced inner linearization that makes Z = v^{3/2} smooth in m. Restoring the OOOO* outer coefficient c ≍ k z^{1/2} ≍ k n^{27/16} produces a W-family phase C theta_2 with C = (3c/2) m^{3/4} ≍ k n^{45/16}, plus an engine-side remainder c E2 ≍ k n^{9/16} theta_2^2. Validated by exact scaled-integer arithmetic through n = 10^{12}. Not a kernel bound.

The nested-floor fifth-letter sum differs from the smooth model e(α n^{81/16}) (or e(α m^{27/8}), or e(α v^{9/4})) by an absorbable error, so K3 can be bounded without forming a W-family. False: Lemma V2 says the pointwise phase defect Y^{3/2} - v^{3/2} is (3/2) m^{3/4} θ₂ + E₂, and restoring the outer coefficient produces the W-family at α = 45/16; Lemma V1 says the outer defect v^{9/4} - z^{3/2} is the K3 phase itself. The error sum is the obstruction, not a remainder. A comparison to the smooth van der Corput sum is therefore circular. Conjecture V is not refuted.

For odd n ≥ 3 with m = floor(n^{3/2}): m^{3/2} = (3/2) m n^{3/4} - (1/2) n^{9/4} + E(n) with 0 ≤ E(n) ≤ (3/8)(n^{3/2}-1)^{-1/2} ≤ (1/2) n^{-3/4}. Substituting theta = n^{3/2} - m into the linear Taylor term eliminates the nested fractional part exactly; the integer m enters the phase linearly with smooth amplitude. Companion gap lemma: m(n+2h) - m(n) = floor(delta) + [ {n^{3/2}} ≥ 1 - {delta} ] with delta = (n+2h)^{3/2} - n^{3/2}, giving constant-gap cells of length about n^{1/2}/h. Both validated by exact scaled-integer arithmetic through n = 10^{12}.

Conjecture HH (the pure amplitude-product model): for smooth monomial-type A(t), B(t) on [0, L] with 1 << A' << A (Juggler instance: A = (3k/4) mu^{9/8}, B = mu^{9/4}, mu affine, A ≍ P^{27/16}, A' ≍ P^{11/16}), the sum |sum_{t≤L} e(A(t){B(t)})| ≤ L^{1-delta}. The minimal crystal of the K3 program: all Juggler-specific structure (carries, defects, nesting) stripped. The known boundary is A' ≍ 1: for A' << 1 partial summation makes the amplitude a tame passenger (the engine and the Piatetski-Shapiro literature); for A' >> 1 no tool applies (Proposition GG). Census: R = |S|^2/L has a textbook Exp(1) profile at P = 10^6, 10^8, 10^10, k = 1, 2 (pure_model_census) — square-root cancellation, COMPUTATIONALLY unrefuted, analytically untouched.

Theorem R extends to the OOOO* kernel K3 by replacing the W-family exponent 9/8 with 27/16 and adding one Weyl step (the scale-invariant copy predicted by the smooth model G(n) = n^{27/8}). False: (i) there are no v-level b-runs — floor(Delta Y) and Delta v have mean and max run length 1 at P = 10^4, 10^5, 10^6, so Lemma R3 cannot be restated with (X,m,Y,v) -> (Y,v,Z,z); (ii) the forced inner linearization (row J-level3-inner-linearization) produces a W-family at alpha = 45/16 > 9/4, past Theorem R's engine line for Step-3 theta-coefficients (the spawned sawtooth has coefficient > n and derivative >> 1 — the Phase-5 wall at a larger scale). Conjecture V (that K3 itself cancels) is not refuted; the Phase-11 probe still shows square-root cancellation. Not a termination claim.

Second-order exact linearization (Lemma G): for odd n ≥ 5 with X = n^{3/2}, m = floor(X): m^{3/4} = (5/32) n^{9/8} + (15/16) m n^{-3/8} - (3/32) m^2 n^{-15/8} - R3 with 0 ≤ R3 ≤ (5/128)(X-1)^{-9/4}, and m^{9/4} = (5/32) n^{27/8} - (9/16) m n^{15/8} + (45/32) m^2 n^{3/8} + R4 with -(15/128)(X-1)^{-3/4} ≤ R4 ≤ 0, by Taylor to third order with the exact substitution theta = X - m in both the linear and quadratic terms. Consequently (Proposition H) the OOO* layer phase v^{3/2}, v = floor(m^{3/2}), equals a degree-(2,1) polynomial in the integer pair (m, v) with smooth coefficients, up to an error of at most (3/4) n^{-9/8}. The integer m enters quadratically with smooth coefficients and decaying remainders — the algebraic brick for the tier-2 (second growing layer) discrepancy attack. Validated by exact scaled-integer arithmetic (scale 10^{60}) through n = 10^{12}. The tier-2 discrepancy bound was subsequently proved (row J-kernel-cancellation, Theorem R).

Conjecture (formerly Corollary Y; withdrawn from Paper B in Phase 26): the class of starts carrying a uniform power-envelope descent certificate of length at most seven has natural density 57/64. Depends on row J-depth7-engine-contracting, still CONJECTURE. The harvest counting program is laboratory-terminal (row J-harvest-counting-terminal). The contraction step (3^4 < 2^7) is unconditional. The laboratory and Paper B certified density is 7/8 (row J-five-step-descent-density, Corollary 6.4). Not a density of starts that reach 1.

Proposition 7.4 of the parity-discrepancy paper (shift-averaged L^2 bound; formerly 'Lemma II' with an overquantified corollary, corrected in Phase 26): let A_1 < ... < A_L be reals with |A_t - A_t'| >= A'_min |t - t'| for some A'_min >= 1 and let x_1, ..., x_L be arbitrary reals. For S_lambda = sum_{t<=L} e(A_t {x_t + lambda}): | int_0^1 |S_lambda|^2 dlambda - L | <= (6/pi)(L/A'_min)(log L + 1), by direct integration (each pair phase is piecewise linear in lambda with real slope A_t - A_t' on at most three arcs). Corrected consequence via Markov: |S_lambda| <= sqrt((L/eps)(1 + (6/pi)(log L + 1)/A'_min)) outside a shift set of measure <= eps — square-root cancellation times sqrt(log L) in general, genuine square-root only when A'_min >> log L (true in the level-3 instance, A'_min ~ P^{11/16}). The former 'in particular |S_lambda| <= sqrt(L/eps) off measure eps(1+o(1))' was false as quantified (the exceptional measure carried an O(log L) factor). The average says nothing about the single shift lambda = 0; it does not make the level-3 kernel 'generically cancelling' in any sense bearing on Conjecture 7.3. Validated by shift_average_probe (mean R = 1.0042 at P = 10^6, 0.9961 at P = 10^8).

Tier-2 bricks. Lemma M: for odd n ≥ 5, X = n^{3/2}, m = floor(X), integer G ≥ 0, Z = X + G: m^{3/2} = -(1/8)X^{3/2} + (3/4) m X^{1/2} + (3/8) m^2 X^{-1/2} + R5 and (m+G)^{3/2} = Z^{3/2} - (3/2)X Z^{1/2} + (3/8)X^2 Z^{-1/2} + m((3/2)Z^{1/2} - (3/4)X Z^{-1/2}) + (3/8) m^2 Z^{-1/2} + R6, with 0 ≤ R5, R6 ≤ (1/16)(base-1)^{-3/2} (positive third-order Taylor remainders). Lemma N: the level-2 gap satisfies g2 = v(n+2h) - v(n) = floor(DY) + [theta2 ≥ 1 - {DY}] with DY = Y(n+2h) - Y(n), Y = m^{3/2} — Lemma B one level up; on constant-g1 cells DY is a quadratic in m with smooth coefficients by Lemma M. Validated exactly to n = 10^{12} (Lemma M, gaps h in {1,2,5}) and on 3800 orbit samples (Lemma N). Bricks for the kernel bound, subsequently proved as Theorem R (row J-kernel-cancellation). Lean covers only the Lemma N floor identity (seq_floor_gap); Lemma M and all analytic content remain human proofs.

Conjecture (formerly Corollary R'; withdrawn from Paper B in Phase 26): Theorem R's bound K_c(P) << P^{1-1/96+eps} holds for every monomial family c^{(r)} ~ k P^{alpha-r} with alpha in a fixed finite subset of (0, 9/8] excluding {1/4, 3/4}, uniformly for k <= P^{1/24}. The Phase-24 argument was proof-by-monotonicity without rerunning standing estimates at any alpha != 9/8. The single intended consumer alpha = 33/32 is now the separate exact row J-w-family-thirty-three-thirty-seconds (Phase 28); every other target alpha still needs its own exponent set and its own c_6. Not a bound for alpha > 9/8 (row J-scale-invariant-R-extension remains REFUTED).

Publication review 9 September 2026: the analytic claim below is not established by Paper B and is retained only as a historical research target. The revised paper gives conditional implications, not this analytic proof. See docs/theory/paper_b_review.md. Historical target: Theorem R at alpha = 33/32 (Phase 28): if c is smooth on (P, 2P] with c^{(r)} ~ k P^{33/32-r} for r = 0,...,4, derivative signs following the monomial pattern (e.g. c = (3k/4) n^{33/32}), and 1 <= k <= P^{1/24}, then K_c(P) << P^{1-1/96+eps} uniformly in k. Every Theorem 5.3 constraint was rerun: M1 deletion costs P^{13/96}; Lemma 3.7 holds at |B| <= P^{11/96}; Lemma 5.2 applies a fortiori (c, c', c'' all smaller than the printed 9/8 sizes); the offset composite is (9369/8192) k|j| n^{-7/32} at ratio 3.711; the zero-offset interpolant coefficient is 1701/1024 with sub-unit B <= 1.2 P^{-11/96}; the middle-band triple (5/4, 41/32, 3/2) uses E^dagger = E union {41/32, 57/32} with c_6(5/4, 41/32) = 1/55. The Corollary R' family remains CONJECTURE (row J-w-family-below-nine-eighths). Not a bound for alpha > 9/8 (row J-scale-invariant-R-extension remains REFUTED). Not a length-7 count and not a Paper B edit.

The OOOO* leftover C θ₂ with C ≍ n^{45/16} (row J-level3-inner-linearization) is absorbed by an X1 substitution into an integer whose first gap freezes, leaving only engine sawtooths. False: X1 lands on I = floor(Y) = v (Lemma Z3), and Y'' ≍ n^{1/4} > 1 so v has no J-runs. For every tested hybrid Q = v - P with P a polynomial in the freezing integers {w_m^3, m w_m, w^2}, ΔQ has mean and max run length 1 at P = 10^4, 10^5, 10^6. Cubing the T1 expansion of z^{1/2} after absorbing the first-letter θ produces a remainder 3 n^{27/8} m^{-3/8} θ₂ ≍ 3 n^{45/16} θ₂, the same leftover. Conjecture V is not refuted. Not a termination claim.

Lemma Z3: the X1 substitution C{F} = C F - C floor(F) produces a usable frozen-gap integer I = floor(F) if and only if floor(ΔF) is constant on long runs, which for unit steps requires F'' < 1. Instances: F = v^{1/2} (F'' ≍ n^{-7/8} < 1) and F = m^{1/2} (F'' ≍ n^{-5/4} < 1) freeze on a window of 400 odd steps at P = 10^4, 10^5, 10^6; F = Y = m^{3/2} (Y'' ≍ n^{1/4} > 1) has mean and max run length 1 (row J-scale-invariant-R-extension). This is the reason Lemma X1 could land on w and the reason the same move cannot land on v. Not a kernel bound.
